title: Scalar extension of affine Proj with its chart maps
statement:
Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, let $R\to S$ be a ring homomorphism, and let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be a commutative graded ring with a ring map $R\to A_0$. Form the graded $S$-algebra $S\otimes_R A$, with homogeneous component $S\otimes_R A_n$, where tensor denotes the usual balanced tensor product with multiplication $(s\otimes a)(t\otimes b)=st\otimes ab$. Let $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}B_n$ be a commutative graded ring with an $S$-algebra structure whose unit map $S\to B$ has image in $B_0$ and let $\beta:S\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ be a graded $S$-algebra isomorphism. Put $\psi(a)=\beta(1\otimes a)$. Use affine Proj [def-nagata-affine-proj], its degree-zero structure map followed by the spectrum map [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to obtain $p_A:\operatorname{Proj}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $p_B:\operatorname{Proj}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}S$. There is a canonical morphism $r_\psi:\operatorname{Proj}(B)\to\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ making the square with $p_A,p_B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(R\to S)$ cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every homogeneous $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, its inverse image of $D_+(f)$ is $D_+(\psi(f))$ and its restriction to that open is the spectrum morphism induced by
$$A_{(f),0}\longrightarrow B_{(\psi(f)),0},\qquad a/f^m\longmapsto\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m$$
[def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. The opens $D_+(\psi(f))$, as $f$ ranges over all positive-degree homogeneous elements of $A$, cover $\operatorname{Proj}(B)$; these formulas uniquely determine $r_\psi$.

proof.text: Construct the irrelevant-ideal inequality directly from the graded-span hypothesis. The completed upstream theorem `AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isPullback_map_of_isGradedBaseChange` then supplies the cartesian square. Mathlib’s `Proj.map_preimage_basicOpen`, `Proj.awayι_comp_map`, `Proj.mapAffineOpenCover`, and cover hom-ext supply the inverse-image formulas, chart formulas, image cover, and uniqueness. The supplied tensor algebra equivalence and the equalities `hgraded`, `hβψ`, `hρA`, and `hρB` give the coefficientwise `IsGradedBaseChange` witness required by that theorem.
